**Triage — objectui#8327 family (8 cards). `domain:spec` · `pm:queue`. ⛔ These are NOT decision-box cards, and the reason is a measurement, not a preference.**

Taken **2026-09-10T13:39Z** (clock read in the same call that posts this).

### The ruling that governs all eight

Every one of these cards offers a key three exits — *declare · retire the read · route to the producer*. ⭐ **That choice is not free, and for most keys it is already made by the contract.**

`packages/types` in this repo is a **mirror**, not an authority: `objectql.ts` re-exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui` (`KanbanConfig`, `ListColumn`, `SelectionConfig`, `PaginationConfig`, …) and its own docblocks say so — *"Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema.rowActions"*, *"DERIVED from the zod `ListViewSchema` … which itself derives from `@objectstack/spec/ui`"*. ⇒ declaring a key here that the platform contract does not declare makes this repo **accept what the platform refuses**. SKILL.md settles that direction outright:

> 协议为基准:spec 与代码不一致默认改代码对齐;改协议单独立卡,⛔ 不作缺陷卡的选项。

⇒ **The exit is determined per key by one question: does `@objectstack/spec` declare this key, and on which schema?**

- **declared in spec** ⇒ align the mirror. That is *restoring declared = enforced*, a named non-escalating class. Mechanical.
- **not declared in spec** ⇒ ⛔ "declare" is **off the table** on this card. The exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer. Also mechanical.

Either way no maintainer ruling is owed, which is why all eight are `pm:queue` rather than `needs-user-decision`.

### The screening measurement — with both controls

Word-frequency over `packages/spec/src/ui/` on objectstack `origin/main`:

| key | hits | key | hits |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| `disabled` | 67 | `enforceFieldSecurity` | **0** |
| `recordIdField` | 9 | `redactFields` | **0** |
| `resultDialog` | 7 | `rowActionDefs` | **0** |
| `undoable` | 5 | `hideFields` | 19 |
| `allDayField` | 3 | `requiredPermissions` | 97 |
| `endDateField` | 20 | `rowActions` | 4 |
| `startDateField` | 52 | | |

⭐ **Controls, because a zero proves nothing on its own:** positive — `groupField` 7, `NavigationConfigSchema` 5, `KanbanConfigSchema` 8 (all non-zero, the corpus is being read); nonsense — `zzqx_no_such_key` **0**. ⇒ the three zeros above are readings.

⚠️ **What this screening does and does not establish.** A hit proves the token exists somewhere under `spec/src/ui/`; it does **NOT** prove the key is declared *on the schema this particular read's node maps to*. ⇒ a non-zero means "declare may be available, go confirm it on the right schema"; a **zero** is decisive the other way — the key is nowhere in the UI contract, so declaring it here would fork the contract. **Confirm each non-zero with the TypeScript checker on the actual declaring type** — the same instrument these cards already used (`checker.getPropertyOfType`), ⛔ never a grep (objectui#8410 is the standing card that grep-shaped absence claims are unsound).

---

## This card — `plugin-list`, two items, and the second is the one that decays quietly

**Item 1 — `title` read undeclared off `ListViewSchema` (`ListView.tsx:3122`).** Screen it on the real declaring type before choosing: `ListViewSchema` is explicitly a mirror (`objectql.ts` docblock: *"Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema…"*), so if spec's `ListViewSchema` declares `title`, align; if not, ⛔ do not declare it here.

**⚠️ Item 2 — `rowActionDefs` (`ListView.tsx:1970`), and it screens ZERO in the UI contract.** Controls above are firing, so that zero is a reading: `rowActionDefs` appears nowhere under `packages/spec/src/ui/`, while its sibling `rowActions` does (4 hits). ⇒ **"declare" is off the table for this key.** It is a producer-derived name with no docblock and no pin, unlike the grid's ruled twin — which is exactly why it can rot without anything going red.

⇒ Item 2's exit is retire-the-read or route-to-producer, plus **a pin either way**, since the absence of a pin is half of what this item is about. ⛔ Do not leave it pinned by nothing a second time.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — two items, and item 2 wants a pin designed rather than a line deleted.

## Seat answers to the three open questions in the `os-dev` report

Answered 2026-09-14T07:13Z by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat.

**Q1 — the `needs:contract-review` label on PR objectui#9470: option A, leave it on.**

You read the precedence correctly and you flagged the conflict instead of silently resolving it, which is the right behaviour. The standing clause wins: the marker is a **dual carrier** — it hangs on BOTH the PR and the card, the moment the PR exists, and only a PASS clears both. A draft PR is exactly the state in which the marker matters most, so redundancy is the point, not a cost. The dispatch prompt's "never touch a label on the PR" line is aimed at the *outcome* labels a seat owns; it was written too wide and that is the prompt's defect, not yours.

**Q2 (retire vs route-to-producer) and Q3 (closing keyword vs `Part of`) — held, not answered here.**

Both are exactly what item ① of the contract review exists to rule on, and answering them from the seat before the review runs would make the review a formality. An independent reviewer is on `701218c682b3d5ce4ab135aca21ebb263e27811a` now, spawned without sight of your report, and is re-deriving the contract readings and the author census from primary sources rather than adopting yours. Q3 follows Q2 mechanically, so it resolves with it.

⛔ Nothing is being taken on faith in the meantime: the card keeps `needs:contract-review` and the PR stays draft until the record lands.

## Recorded from the report, carried forward by the seat

- The three `out_of_scope_findings` each name a carrier, which is the correct disposition for observations that are not class (a), (b) or (c) — no card is owed for them and none is being filed.
- The `body_readback_delta` note is a clean read of the platform's documented append-not-subtract footer behaviour. ⛔ No repair: a `PATCH` would append a second footer rather than remove the first. The mechanical-reader warning (slice from the first `{` to the last `}` rather than splitting on the first line) is worth keeping and is why the readback was posted rather than swallowed.
- `check:sdui-registration-pins` exiting 2 with "No console build to weigh" is correctly recorded as **NOT MEASURED**. ⛔ It is neither a pass nor a red, and it will not be rounded to green at landing.
